why: The new `who` filter keeps only the models lines whoOfLine gives to that part (a character's name for lines 0..n-1, else u.leads). So a part's 'per model' / 'every model' / 'none of these' claims cover just that part, and its sentences follow Select Weapons ('You can select one or more ranged weapons that model has'; 'You must select one melee weapon that model has'). Run in a harness against the live app.html. One character (Mek + Tankbustas): the Mek line is left out, giving 'Tankbusta w/ Two Busta Rokkit Launchas can shoot with one or both' and 'Nob picks one to fight with: Choppa or Smash Hammer. The others: one each'. Two characters (Bigboss + Warboss + Breaka Boyz): Bigboss and Warboss are each judged alone, and the bodyguard line is 'Nob picks one…' without the Warboss's Power Klaw. Made-up case, both characters with two melee weapons: each gets its own 'Pick one to fight with'. An enhancement on the 2nd character doesn't reach this function. When only one part has weapons of a kind, weaponRows passes who=null, and the other parts' lines are listed as 'none of these', which is true. Nothing goes beyond the rules. Latent, with no such unit in either list: (a) whoOfLine gives each character exactly one models line, but 19.04 speaks of 'The last model in that leader/support unit', so the 2nd line of a multi-model leader unit would be judged as bodyguard; (b) the part's sentence still gets the whole unit `u`, whose kw is the union, so useSentence's test for Close-quarters 'for each model in that unit (excluding MONSTER/VEHICLE models)' would give a MONSTER character's keyword to non-MONSTER bodyguard models; (c) a weapon `who` that isn't exactly u.name, also[].name or u.leads leaves `mine` empty, and the line silently disappears (check.js doesn't test this).

`n.attached && !u.leads` keeps only units with a leader or support character attached. The Leader/Support text in data.js: 'for each leader and support unit in your army, you can select one friendly bodyguard unit that unit can lead. That unit will then lead that bodyguard unit for the battle and form an attached unit with it'. So a unit with only a support character (Mek + Tankbustas) is an attached unit, as the code comment says. Attaching happens only 'Before the battle, in the Muster Armies step', so the list's `leads` covers every unit that can be attached. Breakin' Heads needs {all:[Faction: Orks, Infantry], attached:true}, which is the WHEN 'a friendly attached ORKS INFANTRY unit' with nothing added. Harness result: offered to Nazdreg + Meganobz, Bigboss + Warboss + Breaka Boyz, and Warboss in Mega Armour + Meganobz; Ghazghkull and the Beastboss (not attached) are left out. Two characters need no special case. Not judged here: whether a mixed attached unit counts as INFANTRY. That rests on the union `kw` in data.js, not on this function, and the core text on unit keywords isn't in the item.

Enhancement is right: tagOf puts u.enhancement on the line whose whoOfLine is u.enhOn, else on line 0. Harness: Bigboss + Warboss + Breaka Boyz gives 'Warboss · Kunnin’ But Brutal' on the 50mm base and a plain Bigboss. The same unit without enhOn puts it on Bigboss. One character: 'Warboss in Mega Armour · Follow Me Ladz'. Warlord is the unclear part: `i === 0 && u.warlord` always writes 'Warlord' on the first character. The data has only a unit-level `warlord` flag, and nothing says the Warlord of a two-character unit is the first one. The Warlord is a model (Da Boss: 'if a model with this ability is your WARLORD'). A list whose Warlord is the Warboss in Bigboss + Warboss + Breaka Boyz would get 'Bigboss · Warlord'. To decide this I'd need which character the New Recruit list marks as Warlord, e.g. a `warlordOn` field like `enhOn`. No live effect: both lists' Warlords are single-model units. bug: own() writes u.short on every line whose name differs from u.name. So when an attached unit's first character has a short name, every other character's base gets the first one's short name. Made-up case with short 'Boss': the Warboss base reads 'Boss · Kunnin’ But Brutal'.
fix: In tagOf: `u.warlord && (u.warlordOn ? whoOfLine(u, i) === u.warlordOn : i === 0) ? 'Warlord' : ''`. In data.js, set `warlordOn: '<character name>'` whenever the Warlord isn't the first character (the same convention as enhOn). In own, use u.short only on line 0: `const own = (l, words, i) => [i > 0 || l.name === u.name || !u.short ? baseName(l.name) : u.short].concat(words).join(' · ');` and call it as `own(lines[0], tagOf(0), 0)` and `own(l, tagOf(i), i)`.

why: The changed rows match the data. 'Attached' has one line per charsOf entry: 'supports' when that character's support flag is set, else 'leads'. Harness: 'Bigboss supports Breaka Boyz' and 'Warboss leads Breaka Boyz'; a made-up unit with also[0].support gives 'Bigboss leads… / Warboss supports…'. 'Enhancements' says 'Kunnin’ But Brutal 20 pts on Warboss' through enhOn, else the first character. The rest was checked against the rule texts in data.js. The Reserves line matches 20.01 ('(including those embarked within TRANSPORTS…) cannot exceed 50% of your points limit') and 20.03 ('from the second battle round onwards'; destroyed at the end of round 3, except 'Units embarked within TRANSPORTS that have made an ingress move' and 'Repositioned units'). Deep Strike and Scouts both say 'if every model in this/a unit has this ability', which is everyModel. The start-of-round and per-battle rows match their texts (Da Boss 'At the start of the battle round'; War Cry; Bomb Squig 'twice per battle, per unit'; Insane Bravery). bug: the Warlord row uses unitLink, i.e. shortName, which is the first character plus ' · ' + u.enhancement. A two-character Warlord unit with enhOn would read 'Bigboss · Kunnin’ But Brutal': the enhancement sits next to a character enhOn says doesn't have it, and the first character is named as Warlord (the same missing warlordOn as in proxyLines). No live effect: the Warlords are Warboss and Ghazghkull Thraka. Minor: the reserves sentence drops 20.01's '(excluding FORTIFICATIONS)'; neither list has a fortification. The rules' verb for both kinds is 'lead' ('That unit will then lead that bodyguard unit'), so 'supports' is the app's own label for the Support holder. 'Bigboss (Support) leads Breaka Boyz' would be the literal form.
fix: Warlord row: `row('Warlord', warlord.map(u => u.leads ? linkTo('unit', u.id, u.warlordOn || u.short || u.name) : unitLink(u)).join(', '))`, with the same `warlordOn` data field as in the proxyLines fix. Optional, for literal wording: `(c.support ? ' (Support) leads ' : ' leads ')`.
